hints.title: Negative Pair Multiplication Insight
hints.text: The maximum product of three numbers can arise either from the three largest positive numbers or from two large negative numbers multiplied by the largest positive.

hints.title: Top Three And Bottom Two Extremes Invariant
hints.text: Tracking only the three largest numbers and the two smallest numbers during a single traversal provides all candidates required to determine the optimal product.

hints.title: Single Pass Extremum Comparison Procedure
hints.text: Initialize variables for the three largest and two smallest values. Iterate through the array once, updating the values appropriately. Compare the product of the three largest numbers against the product of the two smallest numbers and the single largest number. Return the greater product.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing all triplets requires O(N^3) time, while sorting takes O(N log N) time and allocates extra space depending on the sorting implementation.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Maintaining five tracking variables in a single linear pass achieves optimal O(N) time and true O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should explicitly mention negative numbers (product of two negatives is positive) and avoid unnecessary sorting.
